closure_explanation: Theorem 6.4's proof uses Theorem 6.3 (iteration count), the universal computation model (eq:required_time) with V_i continuous and non-decreasing (Section 3 theorem), and Lemma lemma:min_inf (second set) for the minimum in tbar_k. Theorem 6.3 is cited from Tyurin & Richtarik (2023); this paper only states it, and its proof (Malenia SGD is SGD with the averaged estimator whose variance is at most sigma^2/S, lines 2338-2350, plus the classical SGD analysis) is formalized here (HetVar, SGDtv). Derived nodes connect the template runs to the iterates (IterExec for Theorem 6.3, Exec64 for the event execution of Method 4 and the time bound). Repository nodes: the universal model, V_i continuity (accepted formalization of Theorem 5.3), the uniform-index lemma and horizon coverage (accepted Rennala formalizations). Excluded: lower bounds (Theorems 5.1, 6.1, 6.2), Rennala SGD results, convex results and examples.

clauses.text: For all i, x: E_xi[grad f_i(x; xi)] = grad f_i(x) and E_xi||grad f_i(x; xi) - grad f_i(x)||^2 <= sigma^2; every computed stochastic gradient uses a fresh independent sample.

interpretations.basis: Any family of distributions D_i can be realized on the product space with the product law; Assumption 1.4 refers to grad f_i, which presupposes differentiability; measurability is needed for the expectations.
interpretations.decision: The per-worker sample distributions D_i are realized as measurable maps g_i(x, xi) of one common sample space with one law; samples are i.i.d. across computed gradients; each f_i is differentiable (grad f_i exists).

interpretations.effect_on_scope: Covers every case in which the paper's V_i is defined.

clauses.text: V_i(t) := int_0^t v_i(tau) d tau.
The number of stochastic gradients worker i can compute in [t_0, t_1] is floor(V_i(t_1) - V_i(t_0)).
A computation started at time s_t finishes at the first time t with V_i(t) - V_i(s_t) >= 1; the algorithm observes the next finishing worker.

interpretations.basis: Time-ordered realization of Protocol 2 with the oracles of eq:oracle_inside_random_heter for methods that wait for the next worker.
interpretations.decision: Finishing times are min{t >= s : V_i(t) >= V_i(s) + 1} (none if never); the next event is the earliest finishing worker.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Identical observable behaviour; reused from the accepted formalization of Theorem 5.3.

nodes.statement: Universal computation model: V_i(t) = int_0^t v_i; a computation started at time s finishes at the first time t with V_i(t) - V_i(s) >= 1; a worker computing back to back from t_0 completes floor(V_i(t_1) - V_i(t_0)) gradients by t_1.

clauses.justification: Method 4 lines 7-11 and the oracle of the heterogeneous setup.
clauses.text: The next finishing worker j returns the stochastic gradient grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,B_j}) of its local function; finished workers are asked to compute again at x^k.

interpretations.basis: Method 4 indexes the received gradients as grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,B_j}); all running computations in round k were started at x^k (all workers are asked at x^k, finished workers restart at x^k, all computations stop at the end of the round), so the point argument is x^k.
interpretations.decision: The environment holds one array of samples per round (xi^k_{i,j})_{i,j}; each event of round k by worker i with count j uses xi^k_{i,j}; the arrays of different rounds are independent and samples are i.i.d.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Identical behaviour for the pinned Method 4; samples are fresh for every computed gradient.

nodes.statement: Heterogeneous oracle semantics: the finishing worker i returns grad f_i(x^k; xi^k_{i,B_i}) at the point it was asked to compute, with the sample xi^k_{i,B_i} of round k, worker i and count B_i.

clauses.justification: (eq:upper_bound) with the convention min{} = infinity, written for general work functions and threshold.
clauses.text: tbar_0 := 0; for k >= 1, tbar_k := min{t >= 0 : ((1/n) sum_{i=1}^n floor(W_i(t) - W_i(tbar_{k-1}))^{-1})^{-1} >= eta} (infinity if the set is empty; then all later tbar are infinite); (eq:upper_bound) is the instance W_i = V_i, eta = max{2 sigma^2/(n eps), 1}.

interpretations.basis: Lemma lemma:min_inf shows the infimum is attained. With the convention 1/0 = infinity a zero floor makes the harmonic mean 0 < eta (eta >= 1 > 0), and for t below the previous time all floors are <= 0; so for eta > 0 the set is exactly the set with all floors >= 1.
interpretations.decision: tbar_k is represented in [0, infinity] as the infimum of the set (infinity if empty); the condition is encoded as 'every floor is >= 1 and eta <= ((1/n) sum_i 1/floor_i)^{-1}'.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Identical values for every threshold eta > 0 and non-decreasing work functions W (all floors are <= 0 before the previous time and >= 0 after it), in particular for eta = max{2 sigma^2/(n eps), 1} and W = V.

nodes.statement: For work functions W_1..W_n and a threshold eta: tbar_0 = 0 and tbar_k = min{t >= 0 : ((1/n) sum_i floor(W_i(t) - W_i(tbar_{k-1}))^{-1})^{-1} >= eta} (infinity if empty). Theorem 6.4 uses W_i = V_i and eta = max{2 sigma^2/(n eps), 1}.

clauses.text: For k = 0..K-1: all workers start at x^k with B_i = 0, g_i = 0; while the harmonic mean of the B_i is below S/n, wait for the next worker j, increment B_j, add its gradient to g_j and restart worker j at x^k.
g^k = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n (1/B_i) g_i; x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g^k; stop all workers' calculations.

clauses.justification: Theorem 6.3 bounds the average of E||grad f(x^k)||^2; a uniformly random iterate realizes this average as the expectation required by the eps-stationary point definition.
clauses.text: Output: a point chosen uniformly at random among the iterates x^0, ..., x^K, together with the elapsed time.

interpretations.basis: The while condition of Method 4 with the convention 1/0 = infinity.
interpretations.decision: The stopping rule is checked after every received gradient (equivalently before waiting, since B_i = 0 initially violates it); the harmonic-mean condition with a zero count is false (1/0 = infinity).

interpretations.basis: The while condition stops on the harmonic mean of the counts, which depends on which workers finish first.
interpretations.decision: The iterates of Method 4 depend on the event order through the exit counts B^k (unlike Rennala SGD, whose iterates do not depend on the computation dynamics).
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Recorded in the dependencies of x^k.

interpretations.basis: Time complexity is the time at which an eps-stationary random point is available.
interpretations.decision: Random-iterate output and elapsed time are part of the output.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Standard realization, as in the accepted Theorem 5.3 formalization.

nodes.statement: Method 4 (Malenia SGD): for k = 0..K-1: ask all workers to compute at x^k; set g_i = 0, B_i = 0; while ((1/n) sum_i 1/B_i)^{-1} < S/n: wait for the next worker j, B_j += 1, g_j += grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,B_j}), ask worker j again at x^k; then g^k = (1/n) sum_i g_i/B_i, x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g^k, stop all workers.

classification.reason: Equivalent SGD form of Method 4 stated in the convex appendix (line 2338) and used for Theorem 6.3.

clauses.justification: Line 2338: Malenia SGD is equivalent to classical SGD with this step.
clauses.text: x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g^k with g^k = (1/n) sum_j (1/B^k_j) sum_{i=1}^{B^k_j} grad f_j(x^k; xi^k_{j,i}), independent sample arrays per iteration; one oracle call per iteration; output a uniformly random iterate.

interpretations.basis: In Method 4 the counts at the exit of the while loop satisfy exactly this condition; in the universal model with deterministic v_i they are deterministic; the analysis uses only sum_j 1/B_j <= n^2/S (line 2348).
interpretations.decision: Theorem 6.3 is formalized for every schedule of counts B^k with all B^k_i >= 1 and ((1/n) sum_i 1/B^k_i)^{-1} >= S/n.

interpretations.basis: The template measures oracle calls; Method 4 observes one event per received gradient and the number of events per round is not bounded by S (it depends on the computation powers); the source headline is the time, which is kept as a bound on the returned clock.
interpretations.decision: The template run is executed for any number of worker-completion events calls >= sum_i floor(V_i(tbar_K)), which bounds the number of gradients all workers can complete by time tbar_K.
interpretations.effect_on_scope: Every run of Method 4 that finishes by tbar_K is covered; the extra calls are idle.
